scope.notes: Read SPEC, the pool JSON (115 items: 46 s, 56 m, 7 r, 3 d, 3 w) and the full dump (208 expanded questions; dump collapses colliding ids). Content of the English is largely sound: every s-item distractor checked and wrong; cloze sets have one answer. BLOCKER (infrastructure, not patchable by item id): question id = sha1(skill|kind|q) so m-items with the same stem collide: 'Which sentence is correct?' x4 (all id 0065abb9: last-night film, She's already left, snowy since Tuesday, Have you ever ridden a camel) and 'Which sentence has a mistake?' x2 (id 67da9294: Rome last year, never rode a horse). Duplicate question ids; the dump shows them under one header. Author must give each a unique stem, e.g. 'Which sentence is correct? (film, last night)' / 'Which sentence uses the short form 's correctly?' / 'Which sentence about Tuesday is correct?' / 'Which question about experience is correct?' / 'Which sentence has a mistake in the time expression?' / '... in the verb form?'; or builder must hash q+options. MAJOR (systemic): the cloze/pick hint 2 is the Korean rule text, and in ~25 s-items the rule states the answer outright (e.g. 'eat의 과거분사는 eaten이고', 'draw-drew-drawn', 'know의 과거분사는 known', 'has gone to'), so the hint gives the cloze answer away. Needs separate hint wording that does not name the key form (rule is fine for the explanation). Also: reading-question answer positions follow a rotating pattern (a descends by one each question, e.g. 1,0,3,2,1 / 3,2,1,0 / 0,3,2,1 in all 10 passages), which is guessable. Repetition: ~22 of 46 s-items are the same frame 'has/have + irregular participle + object' (draw, write, take, break, grow, ride, hide, choose, teach, do, hear, sing, spend, rise, meet, bring, win, lose, become, eat) with word swaps (6 tagged sub:true by patches, SPEC cap 5%); been/gone contrast asked 5 times (Tom gone to Paris, Ann post office, Busan, Mina not here, She has gone to London); since/for about 20 of 115; 'ride' appears twice. Topics narrow (home/school chores); little on 'How often/so far/recently/lately' or have been -ing contrast (correctly excluded at this level). Weak passage distractors (e.g. 'Doctors dislike teenagers') and passages with only detail questions; passages 80-91 words fit M. Not patched: Hobby Q3 and Q5 overlap (never taken a lesson / learns mostly by herself); Nugget Q2 and Q4 share 'escape'; correct option often the longest in m items 'Mia has not traveled to another country', '그녀는 런던에 가 버려서...', Korean translation items.

criteria: Question identity must be unique: never reuse a generic stem ('Which sentence is correct?') for several m items; put the topic or the blank sentence in the stem so the id differs.
Hints/rules must not state the answer form: write a separate hint field for the cloze or keep rules abstract (the rule may name the key form only in the explanation).
Vary the position of the correct option in passage questions randomly; do not cycle a, b, c, d in a fixed order.
Do not make 'a collective noun plus plural verb' (team, family, class, government) or other US/UK-variable usage a wrong distractor; use unambiguous errors.
Do not cite std 9영01-03 (central idea) unless a question really asks for the main idea; tag details 9영01-02, cause/effect 9영01-04, feelings 9영01-05.
A question about 'since X' must say whether the first event counts (ambiguous counting questions are blockers).

Sentence items that differ only in the verb of the same 'has + irregular participle' frame are substitution drills: write at most a handful, tag sub:true, and use varied frames (questions, negatives, time expressions, contrasts) instead.
Within a packet, each contrast (been/gone, since/for, past vs perfect) should be practised through different contexts and formats a few times, not 5 to 20 re-skins.

Passage questions must not reveal each other (e.g. a 'purpose' option that names the later plan; a feeling question next to an 'I can't wait' meaning question); correct options should not be the longest.
Keep the language of explanations consistent (Korean whys throughout; do not mix English whys in one passage).
